## The Methodology

This investigation was conducted by one person using only public records over
approximately 30 days. Every fact on this site can be independently verified
using the sources linked in the [Verify](/validate/) section.

**No anonymous sources.** No leaks. No hacking. No paid investigators.
Just LARA filings, OTIS records, Wayne County Register of Deeds, federal
court dockets, campaign finance records, and LinkedIn screenshots.

The investigation began when a veteran father discovered his children had been
enrolled in a charter school run by a convicted felon — without his knowledge
or consent. A friend and fellow veteran began examining the public record to
help document what they found. What started as helping a friend navigate a
custody dispute became a 30-day investigation that uncovered a network of
convicted felons, shell entities, and judicial conflicts — all funded by
public education dollars.

## How This Site Works

This site is generated from a [git repository](https://git.primals.eco/publicRecord/detroit).
Every document added to the repo triggers an automatic rebuild. Every commit
is timestamped and hashed. If you clone the repo, you have the complete
evidence package with full provenance.

The site itself runs on [ecoPrimals](https://sporeprint.primals.eco)
infrastructure — the same system used for sovereign scientific computing and
open-source development. It cannot be taken down by anyone named in the
investigation.

## Why This Way

This is an ecoPrimals project, and ecoPrimals has a principle:
**[reality owns itself](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/sovereign-science/)**.

In science, truth comes from data and reproducibility — not from credentials,
authority, or institutional backing. A result is real because the computation
passes, not because someone important says so. The
[atlasHugged essays](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/) develop
this argument across twelve documents, from
[Le Guin's Omelas](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/the-city-of-omelas/)
to the
[copyleft covenant](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/the-many-rooms/).

In law, truth is an absolute defense. You cannot be liable for defamation if
what you published is true. This site applies the same standard the
ecosystem applies to science: **every claim resolves to a primary source**.
Not because we say so — because you can check.

The site's credibility comes from the reproducible evidence — not from who
compiled it. **One person, public records, 30 days.**

We don't cite authority. We cite LARA filing numbers, OTIS records, Wayne County
Register of Deeds documents, and federal court dockets. The investigation is
reproducible. The evidence is cloneable. The corrections are public.

If any of it is wrong, [tell us](/contact/) — truth matters more than being right.
And the [correction history](https://git.primals.eco/publicRecord/detroit)
becomes part of the public record, because
[discovery is local](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/discovery-is-local/)
but the substrate — the facts themselves — belongs to everyone.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Case | **2:26-cv-10917** |
| Court | U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Michigan |
| Filed | 2026 |
| Plaintiff | Bryant (pro se) |
| Defendants | {{ actor(key="miller") }}, Wayne County, others |
| Claims | § 1983 — due process, judicial misconduct |

## Why This Matters

- Bryant independently identified **{{ actor(key="miller") }}** as a problem
- Same judge who served as Board Chair of Banks' {{ entity(key="anchor_rock") }}
- Same judge under [JTC complaint](/network/judges/cylenthia-miller/)
- Same judge up for election **November 3, 2026**
- A second, independent litigant corroborates the pattern of judicial misconduct

## Triangulation with Federal Packet and JTC Complaints

Bryant's case establishes that Miller's misconduct is not isolated to one litigant. When combined with:

| Source | Connection |
|--------|------------|
| Complainant's separate Ingham County civil case | Independent legal challenge to enterprise |

| JTC complaints | Ethical violations — airport gun, infant murder dismissal, practicing law while judge |
| [Institutional Capture](/analysis/institutional-capture/) analysis | Miller as captured court actor |

...it creates a **triangulation** that no single case can be dismissed as a "disgruntled litigant."

See also: [RICO Pattern](/analysis/rico-pattern/) — judicial cover layer.

## 36th District Court — Bradley-Baskin {{ confidence(level="reported") }} Indictment (Context)

The 36th District Court — where **three Banks-network judges** sit ({{ actor(key="yancey") }}, {{ actor(key="adam_sabree") }}, {{ actor(key="sean_perkins") }}) — is also where **Judge Andrea Bradley-Baskin** was federally indicted in **January 2026** for allegedly embezzling hundreds of thousands of dollars from incapacitated wards.

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| Indictment date | January 30, 2026 |
| Court | 36th District Court (Detroit) |
| Charges | Conspiracy to commit wire fraud, money laundering, false statement to federal agent |
| Allegations | Used $70,000 in ward funds for bar ownership stake; ward-estate money for Ford Expedition lease |
| Status | Removed from docket; pleaded not guilty |

**This is not a Banks-network connection.** Bradley-Baskin is a separate judge on the same court. The indictment establishes the broader institutional environment — a court where fiduciary abuse of vulnerable wards is alleged at the judicial level.

Sources: {{ source(key="doj", path="/usao-edmi/pr/sitting-judge-and-three-others-charged-scheme-steal-hundreds-thousands-dollars", label="USAO-EDMI press release") }}, {{ source(key="freep", path="/story/news/local/michigan/wayne/2026/01/30/wayne-county-judge-andrea-bradley-baskin-embezzlement/88432584007/", label="Jan 30, 2026") }}

## Summary

{{ actor(key="banks") }} and {{ actor(key="holland") }} have operated as a **cohabitating domestic and economic unit** for at least 20 years. They share a residential address, jointly own real property, co-lead a private foundation, and are connected through a trust that places Holland in control of Banks' primary asset.

This is not inference. It is the documented record of two convicted felons who together hold **every officer and financial position** in a network of entities receiving millions in public education funding.

## The Property Chain {{ confidence(level="verified") }}

Three properties connect Banks and Holland across two decades:

| Property | Owner(s) | Key Instrument | Significance |
|----------|----------|----------------|-------------|
| 21553 Newcastle Rd, Harper Woods | Banks + Holland (JTWRS) | Wayne ROD #2007402847 ($1 QCD, Jun 2007) | Joint ownership since 2007. Concealed in Holland BK3. |
| 21456 Newcastle Rd, Harper Woods | Banks (prior) | Severn warranty deed | One house from 21553. Justin Banks (trustee #2) lists this address. |
| 1968 Severn Rd, Grosse Pointe Woods | Brian Banks Living Trust | Wayne ROD #2024223261 (QCD Aug 2024) | Holland named 1st Successor Trustee (Wayne ROD #2025307266, Nov 2025). HELOC $93,700 (Nov 2025). |

Banks grew up one house from Holland on Newcastle Rd. In June 2007, Banks QCD'd 21553 Newcastle to himself and Holland as Joint Tenants with Right of Survivorship — for $1. That property has been jointly owned for 19 years.

## The Concealment {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

Holland filed five bankruptcies between 2005 and 2014. The critical comparison:

### BK1 — Case 09-46072-swr (2009, Ch.13)

| Schedule | Disclosure |
|----------|-----------|
| Schedule A (Real Property) | 21553 Newcastle Rd — **valued at $65,000** |
| Schedule H (Codebtors) | **Brian Banks** listed as codebtor |
| Outcome | **Dismissed — "lack of good faith"** |

### BK3 — Case 14-51632-mar (2014, Ch.7)

| Schedule | Disclosure |
|----------|-----------|
| Schedule A (Real Property) | **"None"** |
| Schedule H (Codebtors) | **"No codebtors"** |
| Outcome | **$110,305 discharged** |

The $1 JTWRS deed (#2007402847) remained on file at the Wayne County Register of Deeds throughout both proceedings. Holland swore under penalty of perjury that he owned no real property and had no codebtors. The deed proving otherwise was one public records search away.

This is **18 U.S.C. § 152** — concealment of assets in bankruptcy and false oath in bankruptcy.

## The Trust Structure {{ confidence(level="verified") }}

In August 2024, Banks transferred his primary residence (1968 Severn Rd, Grosse Pointe Woods) into the **Brian Banks Living Trust**:

| Date | Instrument | Action |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Aug 2024 | Wayne ROD #2024223261 | QCD: Banks → Brian Banks Living Trust |
| Nov 7, 2025 | Wayne ROD #2025307266 | Trust Certificate: Holland named **1st Successor Trustee** |
| Nov 2025 | Wayne ROD #2025307267 | HELOC: **$93,700** against 1968 Severn |

If Banks dies, becomes incapacitated, or faces a judgment, **Holland controls the asset**. The trust was created six months after Holland's MDOC discharge ("WITHOUT IMPROVEMENT") and one year before the litigation began.

## The Entity Structure {{ confidence(level="verified") }}

Banks and Holland together hold **every position** at multiple entities:

| Entity | Banks' Role | Holland's Role | Address |
|--------|-------------|---------------|---------|
| Purpose Foundation (LARA 803294855) | President + Director | Secretary + Treasurer | 1968 Severn Rd |
| Purpose Group LLC (LARA 803295082) | Sole Member | — | 1968 Severn Rd |
| Banks Strategy LLC (LARA 802070120) | Sole Member | — | 1968 Severn Rd |
| Bank on Banks PAC (#517977) | — | Treasurer | 1968 Severn Rd |
| Brian Banks Living Trust | Settlor/Trustee | 1st Successor Trustee | 1968 Severn Rd |

Every entity. Same two people. Same home address. Zero independent oversight.

## What This Means for Public Schools {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

Purpose Group LLC — of which Banks is the sole member — takes **72.67%** of MacDowell Preparatory Academy's revenue ($3,936,712 of $4,929,893). The management agreement (Section 5.2) states there are **"No Related Parties or Common Control"** between Purpose Group and Purpose Charter Academy.

Banks is the sole member of Purpose Group AND the superintendent of PCA. Holland — his co-resident, co-owner, domestic partner, and successor trustee — holds the financial positions. That clause is violated on its face.

These are **public schools** funded with **public money**, educating **Detroit children**. Parents have a right to know who controls the money.

## The Tax Lien {{ confidence(level="verified") }}

Banks has a tax lien recorded at **21553 Newcastle Rd** — Holland's address. This confirms cohabitation: Banks uses Holland's address for tax purposes while listing 1968 Severn as his "primary residence" on other filings.

Wayne County ROD records show Banks at both addresses across a 15-year period.

## Verify

- Wayne ROD: 21553 Newcastle Rd — QCD #2007402847 (Banks → Banks + Holland JTWRS, $1, Jun 2007)
- Wayne ROD: 1968 Severn Rd — QCD #2024223261 (Banks → Trust, Aug 2024)
- Wayne ROD: Trust Certificate #2025307266 (Holland as 1st Successor Trustee, Nov 2025)
- PACER E.D. Mich: Cases 09-46072-swr and 14-51632-mar (compare Schedule A)
- {{ source(key="lara_cofs", query="Entity 803294855") }} (Purpose Foundation)
- {{ source(key="lara_cofs", query="Entity 803295082") }} (Purpose Group LLC)
- {{ source(key="mdoc_otis", query="MDOC #443789") }}

## How to Read This Page

Every entity listed below is a public record in the [Michigan LARA Business Entity Search](https://mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us/search/business). Entity IDs are provided so anyone can verify. Officer names, addresses, and filing dates come directly from LARA annual reports and formation documents — all public records under Michigan law.

We focus on **business addresses** and **registered agent addresses** (which are legally required to be public for service of process). We do not publish residential addresses for peripheral individuals.

**Source notation:** "LARA [Entity ID]" means the data comes from Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs business entity filings. You can verify any entity by searching [mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us](https://mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us/search/business) with the Entity ID number.

---

## The Purpose Empire — Three Entities, One Man

Brian Banks controls **three** "Purpose"-branded entities. Together they form the corporate infrastructure for his charter school operation.

| Entity | LARA ID | Type | Filed | Status | Agent |
|--------|---------|------|-------|--------|-------|
| Purpose Charter Academy | 900072324 | Nonprofit Corp | 07/31/2025 | Active | Brian Banks |
| The Purpose Group, LLC | 803295082 | LLC | 11/14/2024 | Active | Brian Banks |
| Purpose Foundation | 803294855 | Nonprofit Corp | 12/09/2024 | Active | Brian Banks |

**Purpose Charter Academy** is registered at **10101 E. Canfield, Detroit MI 48214** — the school address. The Purpose Group LLC is registered at the same address. Purpose Foundation is registered at Banks's personal address.

### The PCA Board of Directors (LARA Filing)

This is the board that governs a charter school serving Detroit's children:

| Officer | Title | Significance |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| **Cylenthia Latoye Miller** | President, Director | Identity under investigation |
| **Latisha Johnson** | Secretary | Detroit City Council Member (District 2). Her election was supported by Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit Leaders — the dark money vehicle that fought the journalist exposing Banks. [See below.](#the-three-named-dark-money-vehicle) |
| **Devin Hutchings** | Treasurer | Owns DB Strategies LLC and DB Athletics LLC (LARA 802710175, 802715414). Based in Ypsilanti, not Detroit. |
| **Major Clora** | Director | Previously operated American Motor Coach Inc (LARA 800526511, dissolved). |
| **Lamar Moreland** | Director | **Banks's current litigation attorney.** Moreland represents Banks in civil proceedings. He is simultaneously a director of Banks's charter school. This dual role — attorney and board member — raises conflict of interest concerns under MRPC 1.7. |

Banks is the **registered agent** but does not appear as a named officer. He controls the entity through agent status while the board provides institutional cover.

## The Three-Named Dark Money Vehicle

**Save Detroit Jobs** is a single nonprofit corporation operating under **three different names**:

| Name | Registration Date | Expiration |
|------|-------------------|------------|
| Save Detroit Jobs | 09/08/2016 (original filing) | — |
| Impact Detroit | 09/07/2018 (assumed name) | 12/31/2028 |
| **Detroit Leaders** | 08/10/2021 (assumed name) | 12/31/2026 |

LARA Entity ID: **802002459**. All three names are registered on the same entity.

**Who formed it:** The registered agent is **The Corporation Company** (a professional formation service). The mailing address is **201 Townsend Street, Suite 900, Lansing MI 48933** — the office of **Dykema Gossett PLLC**, Michigan's largest law firm. The entity email is `compliance@dykema.com`.

Michigan's largest law firm set up the dark money vehicle that was used to fight journalists reporting on Banks's network.

## LARA Compliance Issues

The following are potential compliance issues under Michigan's business entity statutes, identified from public LARA filings. These are questions — not accusations. The appropriate bodies to investigate are LARA, the Attorney General's Charitable Trust Section, and the IRS.

### 1. Annual Report Failures (MCL 450.2911 / MCL 450.4207)

Multiple entities in the network have "Not Good" standing for failure to file annual reports, including entities that received or disbursed political funds:

| Entity | Standing | Annual Report Due | Status |
|--------|----------|-------------------|--------|
| Right Turn Project | Not Good | 10/01/2019 | Dissolved (12/01/2021) |
| Banks Powerwashing LLC | Not Good | — | Inactive since 2016 |
| Free Flow Gutter Protection | Not Good | — | Inactive since 2026 |
| Ross Catering Events of Excellence | Not Good | — | Inactive since 2010 |
| Detroiters for Good Government | Not Good | — | Inactive since 2020 |

### 2. Nonprofit Self-Dealing (MCL 450.2545a)

The Right Turn Project's Treasurer (Carlton Ross) is connected to the vendor (Ross Catering) that received campaign payments. Michigan Nonprofit Corporation Act § 545a requires that transactions involving a director's or officer's financial interest be disclosed and approved by disinterested directors. There is no indication this occurred.

### 3. Dissolved Entity Operations

The Right Turn Project was dissolved December 1, 2021. Under MCL 450.2831, dissolved corporations may only wind up affairs and liquidate assets — they may not conduct new business. Any transactions after dissolution raise compliance questions.

### 4. Convicted Felon as Nonprofit Officer

Joseph Holland (MDOC #443789, convicted cocaine dealer) served as President and Registered Agent of the Right Turn Project and currently serves as Treasurer and Secretary of Purpose Foundation. While Michigan law does not categorically prohibit convicted felons from serving as nonprofit officers, organizations receiving public funds or serving vulnerable populations (children) face additional scrutiny.

### 5. Unauthorized Practice of Law Concerns

Banks operated **Serenity Guardianship Services Inc** (LARA 802290962) as a for-profit corporation from 2019-2023, serving as sole officer. Guardianship work in Michigan involves petitioning courts, managing wards' legal rights, and filing accountings — activities that constitute the practice of law under MCL 450.681. Banks was never admitted to any bar.

### 6. Entity Formation Patterns

The dissolve-and-reform pattern (Custom Promotions Inc dissolved February 2022 → Custom Promotions LLC filed May 2022) may be used to shed liabilities while maintaining brand continuity. The three-name dark money vehicle (Save Detroit Jobs → Impact Detroit → Detroit Leaders) allows the same entity to operate under different public identities for different audiences.

---

## How to Verify

Every entity on this page can be verified at [Michigan LARA Business Entity Search](https://mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us/search/business):

1. Go to the search page
2. Enter the Entity ID number in the search field
3. Select "Entity ID" as the search type
4. All officer names, addresses, filing dates, and assumed names are publicly displayed

This is not a dossier. It is an index of public records with analysis of what those records reveal when connected.

The [Michigan Online Educator Certification System (MOECS)](https://mdoe.state.mi.us/MOECS/PublicCredentialSearch.aspx) is the public database where anyone can verify whether a Michigan educator holds a valid teaching certificate, administrator certification, or permit — and which grade levels and subjects each endorsement covers. {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

On **September 26, 2026**, every name listed on MacDowell Preparatory Academy's public staff roster ([macdowellprep.com/about/](https://www.macdowellprep.com/about/)) was searched in MOECS. The audit found that **only 2 of 14 instructional staff members** are properly credentialed **and** correctly placed for their teaching assignment. {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

## Staff Roster Results {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

### Administration — 4 positions ($603,000/year combined)

| Role | MOECS Status | Indicator |
|------|--------------|-----------|
| Superintendent/CAO (Brian Banks) | Convicted felon (ICHAT SID 2029469K). School Administrator certificate only — no teaching credential. | ❌ |
| Dean of Scholars + Culture (Cameron Coleman) | Standard teaching certificate **expired 6/30/2026**. No administrator certification for Dean role. | ⏳ |
| Dean of Academics (Kellie M Stevens) | Standard teaching certificate (K-5/K-8 elementary). **No administrator certification** for Dean role. | ⚠️ |
| Dean of Operations + 8th Grade Teacher (Chalcee Norwood) | **Not found** in MOECS public search — 91 "Norwood" results searched, no match for "Chalcee". Zero credentials discoverable. | ❌ |

### Instructional Staff

| Role | MOECS Status | Indicator |
|------|--------------|-----------|
| Kindergarten (Rachel Webb) | Holds Secondary **English/Journalism 6-12** certification. Zero elementary endorsement. Teaching kindergarten with a high school certificate. | ⚠️ |
| Kindergarten (Lakeisha Bates) | **"No matches found"** in MOECS. Zero credentials. | ❌ |
| 3rd Grade (Alana Hubbell) | Daily Substitute Permit issued through **Escuela Avancemos** — a different school. | 🔶 |
| 5th Grade (Ashlie Spencer) | Daily Substitute Permit issued through **Chandler Park Academy** — a different school. | 🔶 |
| 8th Grade Teacher (Volanda Frazier) | Full-Year Basic Substitute permit only — no standard teaching certificate. Assigned as full-time Teacher of Record. | ⚠️ |
| 2 instructional staff | Properly credentialed **and** correctly placed for their assignment. | ✅ |
| 2 staff | Expired or pending credentials. | ⏳ |

**Legend:** ✅ Valid · ⚠️ Wrong endorsement/placement · ❌ No credentials · 🔶 Substitute permit from other school · ⏳ Expired

*Source: MOECS public credential search, September 26, 2026. Staff titles from [macdowellprep.com/about/](https://www.macdowellprep.com/about/).*

## The Rachel Webb Finding {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

> **A kindergarten teacher holds a Secondary English/Journalism certification endorsed for grades 6–12.**
>
> Elementary education in Michigan requires a specific endorsement in early childhood or elementary education. A 6–12 secondary certification does **not** qualify an educator for K–5 instruction under Michigan law. MOECS shows Rachel Webb's only endorsements are **English 6–12** and **Journalism 6–12** — neither covers kindergarten.

## The Substitute Permit Problem {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

Two MacDowell instructional staff hold **Daily Substitute Permits** issued through **different schools**:

| Staff | Assignment | Permit Issued Through |
|-------|------------|----------------------|
| Alana Hubbell | 3rd Grade | Escuela Avancemos — Detroit |
| Ashlie Spencer | 5th Grade | Chandler Park Academy — Harper Woods |

Daily Substitute Permits are tied to the **issuing school** and are intended for **temporary fill-in duty**, not permanent full-time instructional positions. Using substitute permits from other schools to staff ongoing teaching roles is a credential compliance issue under Michigan law.

Volanda Frazier holds a Full-Year Basic Substitute permit as the full-time 8th grade Teacher of Record — a separate but related compliance problem.

## The Law — MCL 388.1763 {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

Michigan Compiled Laws require charter school teachers to hold valid credentials:

> *"A teacher employed by or assigned to a public school academy shall hold a valid Michigan teaching certificate or a permit issued by the superintendent of public instruction."*

**Penalty provisions when violations are found:**

| Statute | Requirement |
|---------|-------------|
| **MCL 388.1763(1)** | A district shall not employ an individual who is not appropriately placed under a valid certificate. |
| **MCL 388.1763(2)** | **50% state aid deduction** for salary paid during the violation period. |
| **MCL 388.1763(6)** | If a school official is **notified** by MDE and **knowingly continues** to employ an uncredentialed individual → **misdemeanor**, **$1,500 fine per incident**. |

When MDE identifies credential violations, the statute requires enforcement — state aid deductions for uncredentialed employment and, where officials continue employment after notification, referral for criminal prosecution.

## What MDE Did {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

MDE was notified of credential problems at MacDowell. Over a **four-year period**, the Office of Educator Excellence investigated **only one name** — Brian Banks — in February 2022. The investigation was **closed within approximately two hours** after OEE Analyst **Katie Schmiedeknecht** communicated that "there will be no need for an investigation."

MDE **never checked the rest of the staff roster** — despite MOECS and the Educator Registry (REP) being MDE's own systems, searchable by any analyst in minutes.

Schmiedeknecht presents at state conferences on the **same credential compliance rules** she is charged with enforcing — including slides stating that *"Any teacher who is not appropriately placed may be subject to a salary deduction based on MCL 388.1763."* Her office failed to enforce those rules at MacDowell while advising the school through the compliance loophole that avoided penalties for Banks.

*Source: MDE FOIA response (September 25, 2026); MOECS public search (September 26, 2026).*

## Verify It Yourself

Anyone can reproduce this audit in minutes:

1. Go to MOECS public search: [mdoe.state.mi.us/MOECS/PublicCredentialSearch.aspx](https://mdoe.state.mi.us/MOECS/PublicCredentialSearch.aspx)
2. Enter the teacher's last name
3. Check: Is the certificate **valid**? Is it **endorsed for the grades and subjects** being taught?
4. Compare results to the school's actual staff roster at [macdowellprep.com/about/](https://www.macdowellprep.com/about/)

Discrepancies between MOECS endorsements and classroom assignments are visible immediately in the public record.

## The Cost {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

MacDowell Preparatory Academy serves **362 students**. Four administrators draw **$603,000/year** in combined compensation:

| Metric | MacDowell | Context |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| Admin cost per student | **$1,665/student** | Michigan state average: approximately **$850/student** |
| Instructional spending | **32%** of budget | Michigan target: **55–65%** |

Administration at nearly **twice the state average** per student diverts public funding away from instruction — in a school where MOECS already shows that most instructional staff lack proper credentials for their assignments.

MacDowell Preparatory Academy is not an anomaly — it is an extreme example of structural vulnerabilities in Michigan's charter school oversight. This page connects the documented facts from this investigation to the broader patterns that enable them.

> This analysis draws on the specific documented case to illustrate systemic patterns. The broader conclusions are the complainant's analytical inference, supported by the specific evidence documented elsewhere on this site.

See also: [Credential Audit](/analysis/credential-audit/), [Funding Flow](/analysis/funding-flow/), [Institutional Capture](/analysis/institutional-capture/), [Words vs. Numbers](/analysis/words-vs-numbers/).

## Five Structural Vulnerabilities

The MacDowell case documents five interlocking weaknesses in Michigan's charter school accountability framework. The first four are structural mechanisms; the fifth is their cumulative effect on students.

### 1. Charter authorization as revenue {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

Michigan authorizers receive **3% of state aid** from each school they authorize. This creates a financial incentive to authorize and maintain schools regardless of performance.

At MacDowell Preparatory Academy, DPSCD (the authorizer) receives approximately **$147K/year** from that authorization fee alone — revenue that continues as long as the school remains open.

*Source: MDE financial reports; charter authorization fee structure. See [Funding Flow](/analysis/funding-flow/).*

### 2. Management companies as extraction vehicles {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

The Purpose Group LLC — Brian Banks' management company — takes a **10% management fee plus all operating costs**, totaling **72.67% of total revenue** at MacDowell.

The fee-plus-cost-reimbursement structure means the management company can never lose money while the school absorbs all operational risk. Public per-pupil funding flows through the school entity; the majority exits to the LLC regardless of academic outcomes.

*Source: MDE financial records; Purpose Group Management Agreement (FOIA). See [Funding Flow](/analysis/funding-flow/) and [Purpose Group LLC](/network/entities/purpose-group-llc/).*

### 3. Credential enforcement as theater {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

The Michigan Department of Education investigated **one name in four years** at MacDowell — Brian Banks — in February 2022. The investigation was **closed within approximately two hours** after OEE Analyst **Katie Schmiedeknecht** communicated that "there will be no need for an investigation."

MDE **never checked the rest of the staff roster** — despite MOECS and the Educator Registry being MDE's own systems, searchable by any analyst in minutes. A [MOECS audit on September 26, 2026](/analysis/credential-audit/) found that only **2 of 14 instructional staff** are properly credentialed and correctly placed for their assignments.

Schmiedeknecht presents at state conferences on the **same credential compliance rules** her office is charged with enforcing — including slides stating that *"Any teacher who is not appropriately placed may be subject to a salary deduction based on MCL 388.1763."* Her office failed to enforce those rules at MacDowell.

*Source: MDE FOIA response (September 25, 2026); MOECS public search (September 26, 2026). See [Credential Audit](/analysis/credential-audit/).*

### 4. Board capture {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

Judges, assistant attorneys general, and politicians sit on charter school boards, providing institutional legitimacy without corresponding accountability.

| School | Board Chair | Role |
|--------|-------------|------|
| MacDowell Preparatory Academy | Judge Tenisha Yancey | 36th District Court |
| Purpose Charter Academy | Judge Cylenthia Miller | Wayne County 3rd Circuit Court |

These are not isolated appointments. The [Institutional Capture](/analysis/institutional-capture/) analysis documents a broader pattern of judges, elected officials, and state employees serving on boards of schools connected to the Banks enterprise.

*Source: School websites; Clutch Justice reporting (September 2026). See [Tenisha Yancey](/network/judges/tenisha-yancey/), [Cylenthia Miller](/network/judges/cylenthia-miller/).*

### 5. Cumulative impact on students {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

Every student at a bottom-3% school with 14% properly credentialed staff is a student who falls further behind. **362 students** attend MacDowell Preparatory Academy.

| Metric | MacDowell | Source |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| Math proficiency | 3% | MDE, SchoolDigger |
| Statewide rank | Bottom 3% (1,443 of 1,488) | SchoolDigger |
| Properly credentialed instructional staff | 2 of 14 (14%) | MOECS audit, Sep 26, 2026 |
| Enrollment | 362 students | MDE records |

The impact compounds annually. Students who enter kindergarten without credentialed teachers and leave middle school with 3% math proficiency carry deficits that accumulate across grade levels — not as a single-year failure, but as a structural outcome of the conditions documented above.

*Source: MDE assessment data; SchoolDigger; [Credential Audit](/analysis/credential-audit/).*

## The Numbers — General Context

The following points provide background context. They are cited as general patterns, not as specific statistics fabricated for this page.

- **Detroit's overall literacy rates** are among the lowest of any major American city.
- **Michigan** has one of the highest proportions of charter school enrollment in the country.
- **Charter schools in Detroit** have a wide performance range — some perform well, many do not.
- **The accountability mechanisms** — authorizer oversight, MDE credential enforcement, financial auditing — have documented failure points at every level in this case. {{ confidence(level="documented") }}

The specific numbers for MacDowell — 3% math proficiency, 72.67% revenue extraction, 14% properly credentialed staff — are documented on this site and in public records. The broader Detroit and Michigan context frames why a single school's failure matters beyond its own walls.

## What This Case Reveals {{ status(level="inference") }}

This is not just about Brian Banks. {{ status(level="inference") }} The structural vulnerabilities documented in this investigation exist across Michigan's charter school sector:

- **Authorization incentives** that prioritize revenue over oversight
- **Management company structures** that extract more than they invest
- **Credential requirements** that exist on paper but are not enforced
- **Governance structures** that create conflicts of interest rather than accountability

Banks is the most extreme example documented in this investigation — **9 criminal convictions**, fake credentials, **72.67% revenue extraction**, **3% math proficiency**. {{ confidence(level="documented") }} But the structural enabling conditions are not unique to this case. {{ status(level="inference") }}

The same authorization fee model applies to every DPSCD-authorized charter. The same management company fee structure appears wherever a CMO operates under similar contract terms. The same MDE credential enforcement office serves every charter school in Michigan. The same board composition pattern — judges and public officials providing legitimacy — appears at multiple schools in this network.

MacDowell is the case study. The vulnerabilities are systemic. {{ status(level="inference") }}

## What This Page Is

This is not about one school. This is about a system.

Brian Banks runs two charter schools in Detroit — MacDowell Prep and Purpose Charter
Academy. Together they serve about 362 children. But Banks operates within a **$288M+/year
charter school system** involving 62+ schools, 10 authorizers, and a regulatory framework
that Michigan's own [Citizens Research Council](https://crcmich.org/wp-content/uploads/rpt409_Charter_School_Oversight-2020-1.pdf)
has called structurally inadequate.

To understand how a 9-time convicted felon runs schools for children, you have to
understand the system that makes it possible.

---

## 1. Who Runs Education in Detroit

Detroit's children attend school in three parallel systems. None of them answer to
the same authority.

| System | Enrollment | Governance |
|--------|-----------|------------|
| **DPSCD** (traditional public) | ~48,000 | Elected school board, superintendent |
| **Charter schools** | ~30,000 | 10 different authorizers, mostly universities |
| **Out-of-district** | ~27% of residents | Suburban public and charter schools |

More than half of Detroit's school-age children attend schools outside the traditional
public district. The charter sector alone handles **$288M+/year** in state per-pupil
funding — public money flowing through privately governed institutions with widely
varying oversight.

### The 10 Authorizers

Michigan allows universities, community colleges, intermediate school districts, and
local school districts to authorize charter schools. Detroit's 62+ charters are
authorized by **10 different entities**:

| Authorizer | Type | Detroit Schools | Location | Notes |
|------------|------|-----------------|----------|-------|
| **GVSU** (Grand Valley State) | University | ~25-35 | Grand Rapids | Largest Detroit authorizer. 78 schools statewide. |
| **CMU** (Central Michigan) | University | ~9 | Mt. Pleasant | Authorized MacDowell Prep (Banks). |
| **Oakland University** | University | 5-7 | Rochester | [2025 Authorizer Report](https://www.oakland.edu/media/Oakland/Assets/psa/files/OU-Authorizer-Report-2025_Final_ADA.pdf) |
| **EMU** (Eastern Michigan) | University | Several | Ypsilanti | Authorized DPSA (Bettison on board). |
| **DPSCD** | District | 7 | Detroit | Authorized PCA (Banks, 2025). |
| **Ferris State** | University | Several | Big Rapids | |
| **Saginaw Valley State** | University | Several | University Center | |
| **Northern Michigan** | University | Few | Marquette | |
| **Bay Mills CC** | Comm. College | Few | Brimley | |
| **Wayne RESA** | ISD | Few | Wayne County | |

**The geography tells the story:** Most Detroit charter schools are authorized by
institutions located **50-250 miles away**. Grand Valley State University, the largest
authorizer of Detroit charters, is in Grand Rapids — a 2.5-hour drive. Central
Michigan University, which authorized MacDowell, is in Mt. Pleasant — 2.5 hours north.

These institutions collect a **3% fee** on each school's state aid allocation
(~$288/pupil/year). For a university authorizing 30 Detroit schools, that's roughly
**$2.6M/year in authorization revenue** — from children they never see.

Source: [Detroit PEER — K-12 Education System Overview (2025)](https://detroitpeer.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Detroit-K-12-Education-System-Overview.pdf), [MCCSA Annual Report 2023-24](https://www.lssu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/MCCSA_Annual_Report_2023-2024_FINAL.pdf)

---

## 2. The Major Operators — Who Actually Runs the Schools

Michigan leads the nation in for-profit charter school management. **61% of Michigan
charter schools use for-profit management companies** — the highest rate of any state.

### Large Chains

| Operator | Schools in Detroit | Type | Scale | Notes |
|----------|-------------------|------|-------|-------|
| **[National Heritage Academies](https://www.nhaschools.com)** | 16 | For-profit CMO | 103 schools, 9 states | Grand Rapids HQ. $1B+ revenue est. |
| **[University Prep (U Prep)](https://www.uprepschools.com)** | 10 | Nonprofit | 3 districts | Detroit-based. GVSU-authorized. |
| **[Cornerstone Education Group](https://cornerstoneschools.org)** | ~6 | Nonprofit | Detroit only | Founded by Clark Durant. |
| **Covenant Schools** | 4 | Network | Detroit campuses | Central, East, Southwest, Spectrum. |
| **Choice Schools Associates** | Several | For-profit EMO | Michigan | Manages Dove Academy and others. |

### Single-School Operators (Like Banks)

Self-managed single-school operators receive the **least oversight** of any category.
With no parent organization, no network reporting, and an authorizer hundreds of
miles away, these schools operate with near-total autonomy.

Banks is a self-managed operator. He is superintendent of both MacDowell and PCA.
Purpose Group LLC (his private company) takes 72.67% of MacDowell's revenue as a
"management fee." There is no external management company to provide a check —
**he is the management company**.

Source: [Detroit Free Press charter investigation (2014)](https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2014/06/22/michigan-spends-1b-on-charter-schools-but-fails-to-hold/77155074/)

---

## 3. Performance — Nobody's Winning

Neither charter schools nor DPSCD are delivering acceptable outcomes for Detroit's
children. Both sectors perform catastrophically below state averages.

### M-STEP 2023-24 Results

| Subject | Detroit Charters | DPSCD | Statewide | Gap |
|---------|-----------------|-------|-----------|-----|
| **Math** | **9.7%** | **10.5%** | **35.1%** | Charters: -25.4 pp below state |
| **Reading** | **20.6%** | **16.0%** | **40.5%** | Charters: -19.9 pp below state |
| **Science** | 15.4% | — | — | — |
| **Social Studies** | 4.3% | — | — | — |

**School Index (composite):** Detroit charter average = 45.8, Detroit non-charter = 45.4.
Essentially a statistical tie.

### Where MacDowell Fits

MacDowell's **3% math proficiency** is not just below the state average — it is below
the already-catastrophic Detroit charter average (9.7%). MacDowell ranks **1,443 out of
1,488** Michigan schools — bottom 3%.

| Metric | MacDowell | Detroit Charter Avg | State Avg |
|--------|-----------|-------------------|-----------|
| Math proficiency | **3%** | 9.7% | 35.1% |
| Reading proficiency | ~12% | 20.6% | 40.5% |
| Revenue extraction to LLC | **72.67%** | Varies | ~0% |
| Credentialed staff | 14% (2/14) | ~85%+ | ~95%+ |

The question is not whether charters outperform DPSCD — the data shows they do not.
The question is **why both sectors are failing at the same rate** while the charter
sector extracts $288M+/year through privately controlled LLCs with limited
disclosure requirements.

Source: [Chalkbeat — Detroit charter M-STEP (2024)](https://www.chalkbeat.org/detroit/2024/10/07/detroit-charter-students-m-step-results/), [Chalkbeat — DPSCD M-STEP (2024)](https://www.chalkbeat.org/detroit/2024/08/29/detroit-public-school-students-standardized-test-scores/)

---

## 4. The Money — $288M+/Year Through Charters

### Per-Pupil Funding

Michigan's foundation allowance for FY 2024-25 is **$9,608 per pupil**. With ~30,000
Detroit-resident charter students, that's **~$288M/year in state aid** flowing through
charter schools — before federal and categorical funding.

| Funding Layer | Per Pupil | Total (30,000 students) |
|--------------|-----------|------------------------|
| State foundation only | $9,608 | ~$288M/year |
| Total revenue (incl. federal) | $12,000-$15,000 | ~$360-$450M/year |

### The Authorizer Fee Incentive

Authorizers collect **3% of each school's state aid** — approximately $288 per pupil per year.

| Authorizer | Est. Detroit Portfolio | Est. Annual Fee Revenue |
|-----------|----------------------|------------------------|
| GVSU | ~30 schools, ~8,000 students | ~$2.3M |
| CMU | ~9 schools, ~2,500 students | ~$720K |
| DPSCD | 7 schools, ~1,500 students | ~$430K |
| Others | ~20 schools, ~5,000 students | ~$1.4M |

This creates a **structural conflict of interest**: authorizers are financially
incentivized to authorize more schools and keep them open — regardless of performance.
A university in Grand Rapids collects $2.3M/year for "overseeing" schools it rarely
visits.

### For-Profit CMOs Resist Disclosure

Michigan law requires charter school financial disclosure, but **for-profit management
companies claim private-entity status** and resist detailed financial reporting. When
a for-profit CMO takes 72.67% of a school's revenue (as Purpose Group does with
MacDowell), the public cannot see where that money goes.

The [Detroit Free Press](https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2014/06/22/most-michigan-charter-companies-don-t-follow-financial-disclosure-law/77199892/)
documented in 2014 that most Michigan charter companies do not follow financial
disclosure law. The situation has not meaningfully changed.

Source: [Michigan HB 6277 (FY 2024-25 budget)](https://www.legislature.mi.gov/documents/2023-2024/billintroduced/House/pdf/2024-HIB-6277.pdf), [University of Arkansas funding study](http://thestarnewsnetwork.com/2023/08/20/study-detroit-charters-get-6202-less-per-pupil-funding-than-traditional-schools/)

---

## 5. The Fraud Pattern — Banks Is Not Alone

Charter school financial misconduct in Detroit is not an anomaly. It is a recurring
pattern enabled by structural oversight gaps.

| Case | Issue | Outcome |
|------|-------|---------|
| **Summit Academy** | Insider dealing, kickbacks, contracts to founders' companies | FBI contacted. Cancilliari fired 2013. |
| **University YES Academy** | $300,000 unaccounted Title I funds | High school closed abruptly Aug 2016. |
| **Michigan Technical Academy** | $16M debt; creditors seized state aid | Charter revoked. **Teachers unpaid** for summer work. |
| **Detroit Delta Prep** | Only 1/3 of budget on instruction; $217 reserve fund | Closed **22 days** into the 2018-19 school year. |
| **Old Redford Academy** | $19M bond debt; S&P downgraded to CC | **Closing June 30, 2026**. Default expected. |
| **Creative Montessori** | Double-dipping: state funds + private preschool tuition | Wayne RESA demanded $65K+ refunds. |
| **W-A-Y Academy** | $73,349 unsupported Title I drawdowns | Federal audit finding. |
| **Banks / MacDowell** | 9-time felon as superintendent; 72.67% extraction | Investigation in progress. Second school authorized. |

**The pattern:** An operator receives per-pupil funding → extracts money through
management fees, related-party contracts, or vendor self-dealing → academic outcomes
collapse → school closes or is restructured → **the children are displaced** → the
operator opens a new school.

Banks's dissolve-and-reform pattern (documented in the
[LARA analysis](/analysis/corporate-network-lara/)) mirrors the broader systemic
pattern. Detroit Delta Prep lasted 22 days. Banks's entities dissolve and reform
within months. The children bear the cost each time.

Source: [Detroit Free Press (2014)](https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2014/06/23/tangled-web-at-two-charter-schools-shows-shortcomings-of-state/77199894/), [Chalkbeat](https://www.chalkbeat.org/detroit/2018/11/29/21108212/if-we-don-t-learn-from-this-one-shame-on-us-lessons-from-a-detroit-charter-school-that-was-set-up-to/), [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/capital-markets/charter-school-sees-debt-rating-cut-six-notches-as-strain-mounts)

---

## 6. Special Education — The Hidden Sorting

Charter schools and DPSCD serve similarly poor, majority-Black populations. But they
do not serve the same children.

| Metric | DPSCD | Detroit Charters |
|--------|-------|-----------------|
| **Special education enrollment** | **16-18%** | **7-10%** |
| **Students with autism** | **22x more likely** | Rare |
| **Deep poverty (Black students)** | More concentrated | Less concentrated |
| **Overall poverty (FRL)** | ~85% | ~87% |

Children with autism are **22 times more likely** to be in a DPSCD school than a
charter school. Students with severe disabilities are concentrated in DPSCD and
Wayne RESA center programs — not in charters.

This means charter schools receive similar per-pupil funding while serving a
**less costly student population**. The money follows the child, but the most
expensive children stay in the district.

When a charter school reports academic results, those results reflect a
**pre-sorted population** — students whose families chose to enroll them, who
do not have the most severe disabilities, and who are less likely to be in
the deepest poverty. The comparison is not apples to apples.

Source: [Chalkbeat (2018)](https://www.chalkbeat.org/detroit/2018/7/23/21105402/why-detroit-children-with-autism-are-22-times-more-likely-to-be-in-a-district-school-than-a-charter/), [CGCS Detroit Special Education Report](https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1757445862/cgcsorg/j2jrvwi3ygzbdb0gvt5c/DETROITSpecialEducationReport--FINALxx.pdf)

---

## 7. Where Banks Fits — Every Vulnerability at Once

Brian Banks operates at the intersection of every structural weakness in
Michigan's charter school system:

| Vulnerability | How Banks Exploits It |
|--------------|----------------------|
| **Distant authorizer** | CMU (MacDowell) is 150 miles away. DPSCD (PCA) is captured. |
| **Self-managed operator** | No parent organization, no network oversight. He is the CMO. |
| **For-profit extraction** | Purpose Group LLC takes 72.67% of revenue. |
| **Weak disclosure** | LLC claims private status. Board is stacked with his attorney. |
| **3% authorizer incentive** | DPSCD collects ~$147K/year from MacDowell. Why revoke? |
| **Captured board** | PCA board = his litigation attorney + dark-money-funded council member. |
| **No credential check** | Felons cannot be barred from education employment in Michigan. |
| **Dissolve-and-reform** | 12 LARA entities. Right Turn Project dissolved → Purpose Foundation formed. |
| **Special ed sorting** | MacDowell serves general-ed population at maximum per-pupil rate. |

DPSCD authorized Purpose Charter Academy in July 2025 — **after** the Free Press
investigation, **after** the Clutch Justice reporting, **after** the MDE investigation
that "cleared" Banks in 2 hours and 24 minutes.

The system did not fail. **The system worked exactly as designed.** Authorizers are
incentivized to authorize. Management companies are incentivized to extract. Boards
are selected by the person they're supposed to oversee. And the children — 362 of
them, 93% Black — receive 3% math proficiency while $4.28M flows to a Grosse Pointe
Woods LLC.

---

## Michigan's Charter Law — National Context

Michigan's charter school law receives widely divergent ratings depending on who
is measuring:

| Framework | Michigan Rank | Assessment |
|-----------|--------------|------------|
| **NAPCS Model Law (2022)** | 30th of 45 states | Weak on authorizer accountability |
| **Center for Education Reform (2024)** | 4th of 45 states | Strong on growth and autonomy |
| **Citizens Research Council (2020)** | Critical | "No statutory oversight standards" |

The gap between these ratings tells the story: Michigan's law is excellent at
**enabling charter school growth** and terrible at **ensuring charter school
accountability**. The law allows rapid expansion (which CER rewards) while providing
no statutory standards for authorizer oversight (which CRC criticizes).

Key Michigan charter law features:
- **No cap** on university-authorized charters (cap expired 2014)
- **No statutory authorizer evaluation system** (only 12 states require this)
- **No explicit oversight standards** — authorizers define their own rigor
- **Weak conflict-of-interest law** — only covers board member relatives (since 2012)
- **For-profit CMOs** can claim private-entity status and resist disclosure
- **2016 Detroit-specific law:** Only accredited authorizers can open new Detroit charters

Source: [NAPCS Model Law (2022)](https://publiccharters.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/2022-model-law_rd3.pdf), [CER Scorecard (2024)](https://2024.edreform.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/cer-charterlaws-scorecard-2024_final.pdf), [CRC Report (2020)](https://crcmich.org/wp-content/uploads/rpt409_Charter_School_Oversight-2020-1.pdf)

7. **LARA entity data**: [Michigan LARA Business Entity Search](https://mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us/search/business)

Michigan school funding follows a per-pupil model. State aid flows to the school based on enrollment. How schools allocate that funding determines what students actually receive. This analysis compares MacDowell Preparatory Academy's spending patterns to state benchmarks and peer schools.

## Spending Comparison

| Category | State Target % | MacDowell Actual % | Delta |
|----------|---------------|-------------------|-------|
| Instruction (teacher salaries, classroom) | 55-65% | 32.1% | **-23 to -33 points** |
| Administration | 8-12% | 19.4% | **+7 to +11 points** |
| Operations & Maintenance | 8-12% | 12.6% | Near normal |
| Instructional Support | 5-8% | 13.6% | Above range |
| All Other | 10-15% | 22.3% | Above range |

The instruction line is 32.1% — well-run schools spend 55-65% on instruction. The missing 23-33 cents of every dollar is going to administration and the management company instead of the classroom.

*Source: MDE financial reports, FY2025 audit data.*

## The Purpose Group Fee Structure

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["State Aid<br/>$4.9M"] --> B["MacDowell Preparatory Academy"]
    B --> C["Purpose Group LLC<br/>72.67% of revenue"]
```

From the management agreement (OCR'd from FOIA):

| Provision | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| Section 5.1 | 10% of Gross State School Aid ≈ $490K/year management fee |
| Section 5.3 | ALL operating costs reimbursed to Purpose Group |
| Section 5.2 | "No Related Parties" clause — violated on its face because Banks is sole member of Purpose Group AND superintendent of the school |
| Registered address | 1968 Severn Road, Grosse Pointe Woods (Banks' personal residence) |

The fee + cost reimbursement structure means Purpose Group can never lose money. The school absorbs all financial risk. Purpose Group absorbs all surplus.

## What $4.9M Buys

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Math proficiency | 3% | MDE, SchoolDigger |
| Reading proficiency | 12% | U.S. News |
| Statewide rank | Bottom 3% (1,443 of 1,488) | SchoolDigger |
| Properly credentialed staff | 2 of 14 (14%) | MOECS audit Sep 26, 2026 |
| Admin cost per student | $1,665 (vs. ~$850 state avg) | MDE FY2025 |
| Revenue to management LLC | 72.67% | Financial records |

## The Self-Dealing Structure

The management agreement creates a structural conflict of interest:

1. Banks is sole member of Purpose Group LLC (the management company)
2. Banks is superintendent of the school (hired by the management company)
3. Banks controls the Purpose Foundation (the 501(c)(3))
4. Purpose Group's address is Banks' home in Grosse Pointe Woods
5. The management agreement's "no related parties" clause is violated by the structure itself

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Brian Banks"] --> B["controls Purpose Group LLC"]
    B --> C["manages MacDowell"]
    A --> D["is superintendent of MacDowell"]
    D --> E["hired by Purpose Group"]
    A --> F["controls Purpose Foundation"]
    F --> G["receives tax-deductible donations"]
    H["All three entities"] --> I["same controller, same beneficiary"]
```

## The Authorization Incentive

DPSCD (Detroit Public Schools Community District) receives a 3% authorization fee from MacDowell's state aid — approximately $147K/year. This creates a financial incentive to authorize and maintain charter schools, regardless of performance. DPSCD authorized PCA despite Banks' 9 criminal convictions and MacDowell's bottom-3% ranking.

## The Pattern Has a Name

If the [Banks enterprise](/analysis/rico-pattern/) feels familiar, it's because it is. The structure maps precisely to two of the most documented models of American political corruption. Understanding which era you're looking at explains why different actors behave differently — and why the traditional tools for fighting corruption (elections, journalism, FOIA) fail against the newer model.

---

## Era 1: Tammany Hall — The Sabree-Kilpatrick Machine

> *"The ballots made no result; the counters made the result."*
> — William M. "Boss" Tweed

[Eric Sabree](/network/political/eric-sabree/) is a product of the [Kilpatrick dynasty](/network/political/kilpatrick-dynasty/) era — Detroit's Tammany Hall. The parallels are structural, not metaphorical:

| Tammany Hall (1860s–1930s) | Kilpatrick-Era Detroit (2000s) |
|---|---|
| Boss Tweed: Grand Sachem of Tammany, never challenged internally | Kwame Kilpatrick: youngest mayor, installed friends and family throughout government |
| Patronage jobs: thousands depended on Tammany for their livelihoods | Kilpatrick "installed friends and family in key government positions" (FBI) |
| Court control: money distributed to judges for favorable rulings | [9 judges across 4 courts](/network/judges/) with documented connections to the enterprise |
| Contract manipulation: padded costs, kickbacks, bid-rigging | "Pay to play" system, extortion of vendors, rigged bids (FBI, 38 federal counts) |
| Controlled elections: voter fraud, ballot stuffing, counting manipulation | PAC machinery, campaign contribution networks, [late-filing penalties](/docs/proof-packet/06b_SOS_PAC_LATE_FEES.png) |
| Real estate acquisition: Tweed became 3rd largest landowner in NYC | [Property transfers between Banks and Holland](/analysis/banks-holland-partnership/), trust certificates, quitclaim deeds |
| Nonprofit capture: Tammany banks funded by city deposits | Nonprofit 501(c)(3)s used as shells for private enrichment |
| "The Tweed Ring was an engineering marvel — money laundering, profit sharing, and organization" | "Criminal activity was a way of life for him" (FBI Special Agent Beeckman on Kilpatrick) |

**Sabree's position** — Wayne County Treasurer — is the exact Tammany role: controlling the flow of public money, sitting at the intersection of property, taxation, and political patronage. In Tammany, the Treasurer position was the cash register of the machine.

The Kilpatrick machine was brought down the way Tammany eventually fell: **federal prosecution** (38 counts, RICO), **wiretaps**, and **testimony from former allies**. The FBI called it what it was: "a widespread criminal enterprise."

**But the machine didn't die. It evolved.**

---

## Era 2: The Power Broker — Banks as Robert Moses

> *"He was, in essence, above our democratic system."*
> — Robert A. Caro, *The Power Broker* (1974)

When the old Tammany model became too visible — when federal prosecutors, wiretaps, and journalists could identify the patronage-for-votes pipeline — a new model emerged. One that doesn't need elections, doesn't need votes, doesn't need a political party. One that operates entirely through private legal structures controlling the flow of public money.

[Brian Banks](/network/actors/brian-banks/) is not Boss Tweed. He is Robert Moses.

### The Structural Parallel

Robert Moses held power in New York for **44 years** without ever being elected to office. He did it by creating **public authorities** — entities that looked like government but operated like private corporations, with private records, independent revenue streams, and legal structures that made their powers irrevocable.

Banks has been building his enterprise for **14+ years** (and counting). He does it through **LLCs and nonprofits** — entities that receive public education funding but operate with private records, no public audit requirement, and legal structures that make the money flow unaccountable.

| Robert Moses | Brian Banks |
|---|---|
| **Never elected to any office** | **Never elected** — controls through LLC sole membership |
| Created **Triborough Bridge Authority** — a "fourth branch of government" with private records | Created **Purpose Group LLC** — a sole-member entity that receives 72.67% of public school revenue with no independent audit |
| Used **parks** (universally loved) to build political capital and deflect criticism | Uses **children's education** (universally valued) — specifically targeting [homeless and juvenile-justice children](/network/institutional/vitti-nicolai/) who have no alternative |
| Authority issued **bonds** — making its powers irrevocable by contract | LLC has a **management agreement** with §5.2 containing false representations — making the extraction contractually embedded |
| "Records were closed to the public" — Authority operated with no transparency | LLC financial records are private — school reports **$0 in staff salaries** because all employees are technically hired by the LLC |
| Controlled through **contracts, legal fees, insurance commissions** — rewarding allies with money | Controls through **board seats for judges**, CBC events for politicians, campaign donations, [PAC committee](/docs/proof-packet/06a_SOS_PAC_COMMITTEE.png) |
| **Dossiers on opponents** — could "disgorge the dark secret of anyone who opposed him" | **Legal threats** — hired defense attorney within hours, told complainant to contact attorney only, went dark |
| "Above politics, above deals — the newspapers and the public believed" | **Pahara Fellow**, CBC honoree, "Dr. Banks, J.D., Ph.D." — credentials not confirmed by bar records or accreditation |
| Pressured **banks, unions, press, and the Church** into supporting his projects | Network includes **judges, politicians, attorneys, and church** (CBC events, foundation connections, [church layer](/analysis/shepherds-and-wolves/)) |
| Made himself **indispensable** — the only pathway for federal construction dollars to reach the city | Made himself **the sole pathway** for federal Title I education dollars to reach vulnerable children |
| Moses **wrote the legislation** that cemented his power | Banks' attorney [Meihn](/network/professional-enablers/meihn-gregory/) reviews the management agreement weekly — the legal framework IS the power |
| Toll revenue from Triborough was a "sure thing" — he could borrow against it forever | Per-pupil funding from the state is a "sure thing" — as long as children are enrolled, money flows through the LLC |
| Used **expert testimony** and technical complexity to deflect oversight | Uses [expert witnesses](/network/professional-enablers/shulman-terrence/) whose business models align with his defense — a [theft-addiction therapist](/network/professional-enablers/shulman-terrence/) and a [TV psychologist](/network/professional-enablers/leno-michele/) |
| Brought down by **the press** (reputation) and **Nelson Rockefeller** (power) | Currently facing: public evidence library, 7 filed cases, 8 federal agency notifications |

### The Critical Difference — And Where the Apologists Are Wrong

The common defense of Moses is: "he built things." Highways, parks, bridges — physical infrastructure that still carries millions of people. The corruption is regrettable but the product is real.

**This defense understates the displacement.** Moses didn't just build highways — he built highways *through* communities, deliberately routing them to demolish neighborhoods he considered expendable. The effects are so pervasive they appear in popular culture without attribution: *Everybody Hates Chris* — where a kid takes four buses and three subways to get to a school a district over — is literally a product of Moses's transit and highway mapping. The school district boundaries, the missing subway connections, the neighborhoods severed by elevated highways — that's Robert Moses's infrastructure, still shaping lives decades later.

People debate whether Moses was "actively racist." As a matter of science, the question is irrelevant. **The functional existence and continuation of these effects is what is known as systemic racism.** You don't need to prove intent. You need to observe the structure.

This is visible across disciplines. In microbiology and anthropology, geographic barriers shape populations without intent: the Himalayas between China and India are so vast they shaped distinct subcultures over millennia. Mountain ranges, rivers, deserts — natural barriers create isolation, and isolation creates divergent populations with divergent outcomes. No one "designed" the Himalayas to separate cultures. But the effect is real, measurable, and compounding.

**Some have chosen that as a blueprint.** Moses built highways that functioned as mountain ranges — physical barriers that isolated communities, restricted mobility, and created captive populations dependent on whatever services existed within the barrier. Whether he intended the racial outcome is a question for biographers. That the racial outcome occurred is a question for census data. That it persists is a question for anyone with eyes.

Banks operates the same structure without the concrete. His barrier isn't a highway — it's institutional. The children at [Purpose Charter Academy](/network/institutional/vitti-nicolai/) are homeless, in juvenile detention, or chronically absent. They have no alternative school. Banks *is* the only pathway between these children and education funding. He doesn't need a highway to create a captive population. He just needs to be the only option available to people who have none.

**Moses built highways and parks. Banks produces 3% math proficiency.** Moses displaced communities to build things. Banks displaces education outcomes to extract money. Moses left concrete. Banks leaves children who can't do math.

### Why This Model Is Harder to Fight

The Tammany model has a weakness: **it requires votes.** Tweed needed ballot boxes. Kilpatrick needed elections. When the public learned the truth — through journalism, through FBI wiretaps, through trial testimony — the machine lost its democratic legitimacy.

The Moses model has no such weakness. Banks doesn't need anyone's vote. He needs:
1. A charter authorization (obtained once, from [DPSCD](/network/institutional/vitti-nicolai/))
2. A management agreement (drafted by his [own attorney](/network/professional-enablers/meihn-gregory/))
3. Children enrolled (targeted: the ones with [no alternative](/network/institutional/vitti-nicolai/))
4. Per-pupil funding to keep flowing (guaranteed by state law as long as children are enrolled)

No election can remove him. No journalist can shame him out of office — he holds no office. No FOIA can expose his LLC's records — they're private. The only tools that work are the ones that worked against Moses: **a power greater than his own** choosing to revoke his authority.

For Moses, that was Nelson Rockefeller.

For Banks, it will be the federal agencies currently reviewing 7 filed cases.

---

## The Pattern Recognition

This analysis exists because the complainant recognized the playbook. Not from political science — from listening to [*The 99% Invisible Breakdown of The Power Broker*](https://99percentinvisible.org/pb/) while driving cross-country. Roman Mars and Elliott Kalan spent all of 2024 breaking down Robert Caro's 1,246-page biography — the most detailed account ever written of how an unelected person accumulates and maintains power over public resources through legal structures.

When you see:
- A sole-member LLC receiving 72.67% of public money
- Records closed to the public
- Expert witnesses whose business models align with the defense
- Judges on the nonprofit board
- The most vulnerable population targeted because they have no alternative
- The operator making themselves the only pathway for public funds

...you're reading Chapter 1 of *The Power Broker*. The venue changed from highways to charter schools. The city changed from New York to Detroit. The mechanism changed from bond authorities to management agreements. But the structure is identical.

The question is whether the federal agencies will be Detroit's Nelson Rockefeller.

### Postscript — October 3, 2026: The Parallel Became Literal

This analysis was published on October 1, 2026. It compared Banks to Robert Moses — the man who built a 44-year empire through **parks**.

Two days later, on October 3, the complainant discovered that Banks sits on the **Belle Isle Park Advisory Committee** — a Michigan Department of Natural Resources advisory body. Mayor-appointed. Listed on michigan.gov alongside the Deputy Mayor of Detroit and two DNR state employees. His biography on the state website lists his "Juris Doctorate" without mentioning he was never admitted to the bar. His committee email address is `brianbanksjd@gmail.com` — a credential he cannot use, embedded in his identity at the state level.

Robert Moses used parks as the foundation of his power — the Triborough Bridge Authority began as a parks commission. Banks sits on a parks committee appointed by the same mayor whose Deputy Mayor now has his 9-conviction felony record in her inbox.

The comparison in this analysis was intended as structural analogy. Within 48 hours, it became a statement of fact: **the man compared to the Parks Commissioner is on a parks committee.**

Source: [michigan.gov/dnr/about/boards/belle-isle/committee-members](https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/about/boards/belle-isle/committee-members) (contact page revised 2/12/2026). Notification sent to all committee members, DNR state employees, defense counsel, and press on October 3, 2026.

### A Note on Rockefeller — And Honesty About Power

Nelson Rockefeller stripped Moses of his power. This is sometimes told as a triumph of accountability. It wasn't. Rockefeller was not altruistic. He was a billionaire governor who removed Moses because Moses was in his way — not because Moses was harming communities. Rockefeller went on to preside over the Attica prison massacre, the draconian Rockefeller drug laws, and an era of mass incarceration that itself constituted a new tollbooth economy. The man who ended one machine built another.

This matters because the pattern repeats: the person who removes the corrupt operator often becomes the next corrupt operator. The reformer captures the same infrastructure and runs it for different beneficiaries. The machine changes hands. The machine doesn't change.

The complainant makes no claim to altruism either. As a scientist, falsity is costly and must be refused. The claim here is narrower: **this specific enterprise is documented, this specific extraction is measurable, and these specific children are being harmed.** The response is not to seize the machine. It is to document it so thoroughly that the machine becomes visible — and then to build something that doesn't require a machine at all.

That is the distinction between exposing Omelas and building a new city.

### The Broader Context — From Exposure to Construction

The complainant's broader work on infrastructure, institutional capture, and what Moses called "tollbooth economies" is documented at [sporeprint.primals.eco](https://sporeprint.primals.eco):

- **[The City of Omelas](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/the-city-of-omelas/)** — the philosophical framework: Le Guin's question applied to infrastructure. Every functioning city has a child suffering in a basement. The question is whether you stay, leave, or build a city that doesn't require the child.
- **[The Loaves and the Fishes](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/the-loaves-and-the-fishes/)** — who gets punished for stealing, who gets fellowships. The bread thief problem: the preconditions that determine who builds and who suffers.
- **[I Own Nothing](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/i-own-nothing/)** — the systemic pattern: positioning yourself as the sole gateway between a population and a resource, then charging rent. The tollbooth economy.
- **[The Temptation of Kingdoms](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/the-temptation-of-kingdoms/)** — the temptation to build institutions that serve the builder. Rent-seeking and open commons.
- **[An Invitation to 99% Invisible and Radiolab](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/outreach/99pi-radiolab-invitation/)** — how infrastructure storytelling informed this investigation.

Detroit is the field validation of that theoretical work: a real tollbooth economy running on children's education funding, identified because the builder recognized the blueprint from a podcast about a man who built bridges. The response is not to become the next Rockefeller. It is to [walk away from Omelas](https://sporeprint.primals.eco/philosophy/the-city-of-omelas/) and build infrastructure that doesn't require a child in a basement.

## The Network Is Not a Hierarchy — It Is a Response System

Traditional corruption investigations map organizations top-down: find the boss, trace the orders, follow the money. This network does not work that way. It is **threat-responsive** — each nexus activates when another is under pressure, routing around the attack.

When Kevin Mok burned Banks's Wayne County police infrastructure, Banks filed false reports in Grosse Pointe Woods — a different jurisdiction, a different police nexus, the same function.

The network has **four nexus types**, each with its own center of gravity, its own institutional protection, and its own method of weaponization.

---

## Nexus 1: Education Fraud — The Revenue Engine

**Center of gravity:** Brian Banks through The Purpose Group Michigan LLC

Banks operates two charter schools that collectively move millions in taxpayer funds through a management company where he is the sole registered agent.

| School | Students | Math Proficiency | Reading | State Rank | Per-Pupil |
|--------|----------|-----------------|---------|------------|-----------|
| [MacDowell Preparatory Academy](https://clutchjustice.com/2026/09/13/macdowell-preparatory-academy-academic-financial-record/) | 362 | **3%** | 10-14% | 1,443/1,488 (bottom 3%) | $15,217 |
| Purpose Charter Academy | 225 projected | *opening 2026-27* | — | — | — |

Three percent math proficiency means roughly **11 of 362 children** can do grade-level math. That is not a struggling school. That is a revenue extraction operation wearing a school's skin.

MacDowell ran a **$967,964 operating deficit** in FY2024-25, covered by drawing down its fund balance. The check register shows **$13,970 in gift-card-labeled payments** in a single fiscal year, including one $9,945 check.

DPSCD authorized the **second school** in July 2025 — citing "claimed improvement at MacDowell." The person who made the "30% proficiency gains" claim was **Nicole Wells Stallworth**, the Board Chair, not an independent evaluator. On a base of 3%, a 30% gain is approximately **three additional children**.

### The Credential-Washing Board

Every bar complaint filed in this investigation corresponds to a board member of one of Banks's schools:

| Bar Target | Role | School | Credential Washed |
|-----------|------|--------|-------------------|
| Gregory Meihn (P65372) | Board counsel | MacDowell | Testified Banks has "integrity" at [TCR 22-12](/evidence/tcr-22-12/) while reviewing false contract |
| Verkeydia Hall | Board member | MacDowell | Licensed attorney who accepted false §5.2 contract terms |
| Lamar Moreland (P55993) | **Board Vice Chair** | Purpose Charter | AAG whose office argued **against** Banks's certificate — then joined his board |
| Tenisha Yancey | **Board Chair** | MacDowell | 36th District Court Judge — Banks ran her campaign ($15,750 via Banks Strategy) |
| Cylenthia LaToye Miller | **Board Chair** | Purpose Charter | 3rd Circuit Court Judge — school serves juvenile justice youth she may sentence |
| Latisha Johnson | **Board Secretary** | Purpose Charter | City Council Member — campaign funded by Banks's vendor Inner Link ($850) |

The school boards **are** the credential-washing mechanism. Legal professionals lend their licenses to make a convicted felon look legitimate. The felon's website lists him as **"Dr. Brian Banks, J.D., Ph.D."** — the J.D. was never admitted to the bar.

**October 4 Update — LARA Confirmation:** The PCA board composition above has now been independently verified through [Michigan LARA corporate filings](/analysis/corporate-network-lara/) (Entity ID 900072324). Moreland's simultaneous role as Banks's litigation attorney **and** PCA board director is confirmed in the state business entity record. Johnson's role as PCA Secretary is confirmed. Banks controls the entity as registered agent while his name does not appear as a named officer — a deliberate structural choice.

### The Purpose Empire — Three Entities (LARA-Confirmed)

Banks operates **three** "Purpose"-branded entities (see [Corporate Network Analysis](/analysis/corporate-network-lara/) for full details):

| Entity | LARA ID | Filed | Function |
|--------|---------|-------|----------|
| Purpose Charter Academy | 900072324 | 07/2025 | The school itself |
| The Purpose Group LLC | 803295082 | 11/2024 | Management company |
| Purpose Foundation | 803294855 | 12/2024 | Nonprofit — Holland = Treasurer |

All three list Banks as registered agent. Purpose Foundation is registered at Banks's home. Joseph Holland — the convicted cocaine dealer who serves as PAC treasurer — is the Treasurer **and** Secretary of Purpose Foundation, listed at Banks's home address.

Banks has **twelve total entities** spanning Detroit, Grosse Pointe Woods, Holland, Zeeland, Clarkston, and Waterford. Details: [Corporate Network — LARA Entity Analysis](/analysis/corporate-network-lara/).

### The Three-Named Dark Money Vehicle (LARA-Confirmed)

**Save Detroit Jobs** (LARA 802002459) is a single nonprofit operating under **three names**: Save Detroit Jobs (2016), Impact Detroit (2018), and **Detroit Leaders** (2021). All confirmed as assumed names on the same entity.

The entity was formed by **Dykema Gossett PLLC** — Michigan's largest law firm. The mailing address is Dykema's Lansing office. The entity email is `compliance@dykema.com`. All three officers list the **same Detroit address**. Full details: [Corporate Network — LARA Entity Analysis](/analysis/corporate-network-lara/).

She bridges Banks to Gay-Dagnogo through shared campaign payments.

**Banks Strategy and Consultants** was paid **$15,750 by Yancey's campaign** and **$20,000 by the Coalition to Regulate Marijuana Like Alcohol**. Banks was not Yancey's supporter — he was her **paid consultant**. She became a judge. Return on investment.

## Nexus 3: Police Weaponization — The Enforcement Arm

**Center of gravity:** Police Chief Todd Bettison

Todd Bettison is the permanent Detroit Police Chief (appointed Feb 2025 by Duggan). He is **also** the Secretary of the Detroit Public Safety Academy (DPSA) board — a **charter school** authorized by Eastern Michigan University. He uses his official city email (`bettisont239@detroitmi.gov`) for board business.

**The police chief sits on a charter school board.** This is the structural bridge between police weaponization and education fraud.

### Active OIG Investigation — September 2026

As of **September 16, 2026**, Bettison is under investigation by Detroit's Office of Inspector General for:

- Calling activist **Jahdante Smith** on August 5, 2026, requesting he remove social media photos of **Mayor Sheffield** with ex-boyfriend Marvin Walker
- Police subsequently **detained Smith and seized his phone** under a separate warrant
- Bettison denied the seizure was connected to his call
- **The FBI is now handling the investigation** (per Free Press sources)
- DPD referred its investigation into both Smith and Walker to an outside agency

The police chief used police authority to protect the mayor's personal reputation. This is the same pattern Kevin's case documents — police power deployed for personal or political purposes.

### Operation Northern Hook — ONGOING FBI Probe

**Operation Northern Hook** is an ongoing FBI investigation into corruption within Detroit city government and the Detroit Police Department. First public case: *United States v. Spivey, 2:21-cr-20490 (E.D. Mich.)*.

Banks's former attorney, **Todd Perkins** (P55623, Perkins Law Group), represented **two Operation Northern Hook targets**:

| Client | Role | Outcome |
|--------|------|---------|
| **Alonzo Jones** | Retired DPD officer | Convicted — 15 months for cash bribes |
| **Carol Banks** | Council staff member | Investigation target |

Perkins also ran for **Detroit mayor in 2025** (4th place, 5.35%). **Gay-Dagnogo donated $750** to his campaign. **Gasper Fiore** (convicted bribery) donated $500.
